text: Which of these is the best reason to write a loop rather than a stream pipeline?
choices: The team is unfamiliar with streams, so the loop will be correct more often.
The result needs to be mutable, which a stream pipeline cannot produce.
The collection has fewer than a thousand elements, below which streams do not pay off.
The computation is not map, filter or reduce — some stage would do a bit of everything.
explanation: Section 26.2.1's test: name what each stage does. If a stage resists naming, the decomposition failed. The other honest cases are needing an index, iterating two collections in step (Java has no `zip`), an early exit conditioned on accumulated state, mutation, and a long body. Team fluency is a real consideration but an argument for consistency, not for loops; and `collect(Collectors.toList())` yields a mutable list.
